keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After 1368 Basalawarmi ruled from Kunming over Yunnan; the page does not describe Guizhou as his territory (Ma Hua attacked from Guiyang in 1381). The Dali district is left out because the Ming conquest of Yunnan page names Duan Shi, the last hereditary Governor-General of Dali, as a separate commander of the Northern Yuan side. No area figure on either page.

ledger.note: 1368: the Yuan viceroy of Yunnan holds the province for the Yuan after the court leaves China. Before the Yuan fell in 1368, he served as Yuan Viceroy of Yunnan; after the Ming overthrew the Yuan, he ruled from Kunming. Ayusiridara Khan later sent a messenger to confirm his sovereignty over Yunnan (undated).

ledger.note: 1381: the Ming invade Yunnan. Some 250,000 to 300,000 Han and Hui Muslim troops were mobilised; Ma Hua attacked from Guiyang while Mu Ying and Lan Yu attacked from another direction (Basalawarmi page). The Hongwu Emperor had sent envoys in 1369, 1370, 1372, 1374 and 1375; some were killed.

ledger.note: 6 January 1382: Basalawarmi kills himself after the decisive defeat of his army. He drowned his wife, ordered his ministers to commit suicide and killed himself on January 6, 1382; his family was exiled to Jeju.

ledger.note: 6 January 1382: the Principality of Liang ends with the death of Basalawarmi and Yunnan passes to the Ming. The combined Ming forces numbered 300,000 men against about 100,000 of his troops. The Dali district under Duan Shi falls separately in 1382-1383.

wars.outcome: Ming victory: Basalawarmi's army (about 100,000) is defeated by about 300,000 Ming troops in 1381 and he dies by suicide on 6 January 1382; Duan Shi's Dali falls in 1382 and its last stronghold, Dengchuan, in February 1383.
wars.note: Ming forces under Fu Youde, Lan Yu and Mu Ying (and Ma Hua from Guiyang); the Ming conquest of Yunnan page gives about 250,000 troops, the Basalawarmi page 300,000.

notes: Written for ea-06-x from the Basalawarmi, Ming conquest of Yunnan and Red Turban Rebellions pages. Cliopatria has no row (its Yuan Dynasty row ends in 1374, and Northern Yuan starts in 1375). Wikipedia has no article for the principality: the Basalawarmi page links to a Liang (realm) article, section Yuan Principality, which was not opened. Start 1368: the Prince of Liang had been Yuan viceroy of Yunnan before; the dossier starts when the Yuan left China proper. The page is silent on the title's grant date and on the year the Northern Yuan khan confirmed his sovereignty over Yunnan (a client relation the Northern Yuan dossier could carry). Disagreements: Ming troops 250,000 to 300,000 (Ming conquest of Yunnan page) or 300,000 (Basalawarmi page); the Dali Duan are on the Ming conquest page a separate commander and realm (last hereditary Governor-General of Dali, defeated in 1382, Dengchuan taken in February 1383, family sent to Nanjing): the Duan governor-generalship of Dali (1256-1383) has its own dossier in this batch, duan-governors-of-dali; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Dali ends in 1259. Not on any page: the status of Kunming or Zhongqing after 1368, the fall of Kunming and the Qujing campaign. Counterparts needing dossiers: yuan-dynasty (ea-06-a), ming-dynasty, duan-governors-of-dali (this batch).
